definition: VACUUM is a set of normative guidance principles for achieving training and test dataset quality for structured datasets in data science and machine learning.
details: The garbage-in, garbage out principle motivates a solution to the problem of data quality but does not offer a specific solution. Unlike the majority of the ad-hoc data quality assessment metrics often used by practitioners VACUUM specifies qualitative principles for data quality management and serves as a basis for defining more detailed quantitative metrics of data quality. VACUUM is an acronym that stands for: valid accurate consistent uniform unified model

explainer.lead: VACUUM is a set of normative guidance principles for achieving training and test dataset quality for structured datasets. It matters because garbage-in, garbage-out data quality otherwise lacks a principled basis.

tiers.eli5: It's a checklist of principles for making sure the data you feed a model is good enough to trust the results.
tiers.practitioner: Gives qualitative principles that serve as a basis for defining detailed quantitative data-quality metrics. Pitfall: unlike ad-hoc metrics practitioners often use, it specifies principles rather than ready-made measurements, so metrics must still be defined.
tiers.paperLevel: Acronym for valid, accurate, consistent, uniform, unified, model; specifies qualitative principles for data quality management rather than specific metrics.

explainer.example: A team checks a structured dataset against the six VACUUM principles before defining quantitative metrics for each.
